uncertain_decisions.component: Further decomposition of the customer-pet-service into separate 'pet', 'owner', and 'visit' microservices was deferred because Visit lacks an independent repository and relies on OwnerRepository, while Owner and Pet entities maintain direct static references to Visit.
uncertain_decisions.reason: Further decomposition of the customer-pet-service into separate 'pet', 'owner', and 'visit' microservices was deferred because Visit lacks an independent repository and relies on OwnerRepository, while Owner and Pet entities maintain direct static references to Visit.

unsupported_assumptions: Assumed there are no runtime dependencies, shared database tables, or foreign key constraints between Vet and Owner/Pet/Visit that are omitted from the static call and repository relation graphs.
architectural_risks: Within customer-pet-service, OwnerRepository acts as a shared data gateway for Owner, Pet, and Visit interactions, which may cause high coupling and concurrency bottlenecks if load increases.
If business demands later require an independent Visit service, substantial refactoring will be required to decouple Owner/Pet domain models from Visit and introduce a dedicated VisitRepository.
critique: The legacy codebase exhibits two distinct structural partitions at the module level. The vet subsystem is completely orthogonal and presents an ideal candidate for immediate extraction. The owner subsystem, however, conflates Owner, Pet, and Visit lifecycle management under a single aggregate/repository root (OwnerRepository), preventing clean zero-cost separation of visits or pets without prior internal domain refactoring.

migration_priority.reason: Complete structural isolation from the rest of the application; zero cross-service static dependencies or data relations facilitate risk-free extraction.
Encapsulates the core business workflows and data model; represents the remainder of the monolith once the vet service is carved out.

notes: Parsed from LLM JSON. Gold labels were not in the prompt.
